text_html: A 78-year-old man comes to the office for a follow-up examination. He has a 52-year history of persistent, progressive action tremors of both hands. Ten years ago, a 6-month trial of primidone and propranolol therapy provided no substantial improvement of the tremors. He discontinued the medications at that time. The tremors gradually have become more pronounced but slower in frequency. He now has difficulty eating and writing because of the tremors. He has no other history of major medical illness and currently takes no medications. His father and deceased sister also had upper extremity tremors. The patient drinks two glasses of wine daily; he says the alcohol decreases the severity of the tremors. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a 5-Hz action tremor in both hands. Activation of which of the following neurotransmitter systems most likely explains the improvement of this patient’s symptoms with consumption of alcohol?
explanation_html:
Educational Objective: Essential tremor is a common adult action tremor that most commonly presents as a bilateral tremor of the upper extremities. Activation of the γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) neurotransmitter system most likely explains this patient’s symptomatic improvement after the consumption of alcohol.

Key Concept: Essential tremor often presents with a bilateral tremor of the upper extremities and is commonly heritable.

Explanation: The action tremors in essential tremor are exacerbated by stress and activity, and they improve with small quantities of alcohol. Alcohol is thought to improve the symptoms of essential tremor due to activation of the GABA neurotransmitter system, which is thought to decrease cerebellar hyperactivity, which contributes to the development of a tremor. The first-line treatment for essential tremor is as-needed or scheduled propranolol.

Differential: This patient with a family history of tremors presents with progressive upper extremity tremors that improve after the consumption of alcohol. The most likely diagnosis is essential tremor. Activation of the GABA neurotransmitter system by alcohol is the likely mechanism that explains the transient improvement in this patient’s symptoms.

Incorrect Answers: A, C, D, and E.

Choice A: Acetylcholine is incorrect. Acetylcholine is a direct agonist at muscarinic and nicotinic receptors. It increases the actions of the parasympathetic nervous system and causes muscular contraction. Activation of GABA neurotransmitter systems is the more likely answer.

Choice C: Dopamine is incorrect. Parkinson disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder due to degradation of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. Activation of dopamine neurotransmitter systems is beneficial in Parkinson disease but would not have an effect in cases of essential tremor.

Choice D: Glutamate is incorrect. Glutamate is an excitatory neurotransmitter that binds to the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) or α-amino-3-hydroxyl-5-methyl-4-isoxazole-propionate (AMPA) receptors. Activation of GABA neurotransmitter systems is the more likely explanation.

Choice E: Serotonin is incorrect. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that binds to a variety of different receptors in the body. Activation of GABA neurotransmitter systems by alcohol is the mechanism that most likely explains this patient’s symptomatic improvement.
